Malaysia Women vs Indonesia Women 1st Match China Women vs Indonesia Women 2nd Match New appointment Delhi Capitals appoint Mahela Jayawardene as WPL Director of Cricket
 by Cricbuzz Staff •     Share Tweet The former Sri Lankan captain will lead the four-time finalists’ cricket operations effective from the 2027 season © BCCI/IPL The former Sri Lankan captain will lead the four-time finalists’ cricket operations effective from the 2027 season © BCCI/IPL Former Sri Lankan captain Mahela Jayawardene has been appointed Director of Cricket of the Delhi Capitals’ Women’s Premier League team ahead of the 2027 season. A statement from the franchise confirmed that Jayawardene will oversee all cricketing matters for the franchise, including ‘team strategy, talent identification, and player and coaching staff development.’
 It marks Jayawardene’s return to the Capitals’ setup after more than 13 years, having represented the team - then known as Delhi Daredevils - across two IPL seasons in 2012 and 2013, captaining the side in the second of those. More recently, he parted ways with Mumbai Indians as their head coach in the IPL, having overseen three title victories in 2017, 2019 and 2020.
 “Delhi Capitals has a strong identity and an exciting vision for the future of women’s cricket. I am delighted to take on the role of Director of Cricket for the WPL team,” Jayawardene said.
 “The competition has enormous potential to shape the future of the women’s game, and I look forward to working with an established group of talented players and an experienced support team. My focus will be on building on the team’s existing strengths, bringing greater consistency to performances and ensuring we continue to evolve and compete for the title. I am excited about what we can achieve together.”
 Co-owners Kiran Kumar Grandhi and Parth Jindal welcomed Jayawardene’s addition, where he will work with head coach Jonathan Batty and captain Jemimah Rodrigues.
 “Mahela's appointment brings an added dimension of experience and strategic leadership to the women's setup. His understanding of the modern game and experience in building competitive teams will be valuable in taking Delhi Capitals Women to the next level. We look forward to seeing his contribution as we continue to pursue our ambition of establishing Delhi Capitals as one of the leading teams in women's franchise cricket,” Grandhi said.
 “Mahela is one of the finest cricketing minds in the game, and his record as a player, captain and coach speaks for itself,” Jindal said. “We are delighted to welcome him to the DC family and look forward to the experience and perspective he brings to the group.”
 Jayawardene will be tasked with bringing his title-winning DNA into the Capitals franchise, who are chasing an elusive maiden trophy after four runner-up finishes in the WPL. The fifth edition of the tournament is set to commence on January 14, 2027, with the Capitals taking the field two days later against defending champions Royal Challengers Bengaluru in Vadodara.
